title: A morphism is an epimorphism iff its cokernel object is zero
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a preadditive category (its Hom sets are abelian groups and composition is bilinear; for instance an abelian category [def-sp-abelian]), $u:X\to Y$ a morphism of $\mathcal C$, and $c:Y\to Q$ a cokernel of $u$ (so $c\circ u=0$, and every $g:Y\to W$ with $g\circ u=0$ factors as $g=h\circ c$ for a unique $h:Q\to W$). Then $u$ is an epimorphism if and only if $Q$ is a zero object of $\mathcal C$ (equivalently $\mathrm{id}_Q=0$).

source.place: Homology, Definition 010B (definition-injective-surjective, line 641: f is surjective if Coker(f) = 0) and Lemma 010C (lemma-characterize-injective, line 653), part (2): in an abelian category f is surjective iff f is an epimorphism (proof: Coker(f) represents z -> Ker(Mor(y,z) -> Mor(x,z)), so Coker(f) = 0 iff every such map is injective iff f is epi). Stated here for a preadditive category with a given cokernel, which is what the same argument uses.
